images.text:
Salesperson: Hello. Can I help you?
Sally: I'm looking for some stylish work wear. I'm looking for essentials and interesting accents.
Salesperson: With office wear, I think comfort is as important as look.
Vanessa: So do I. I don't think they should be too tight or too synthetic.

Salesperson: Neither do I. It will make working easier.
Sally: I think I'd like to look as chic as possible without being overdressed.
Vanessa: I think so too, Sal.
Sally: I don't think just separates will do.
Vanessa: No, I don't either.
Sally: Some mix and match outfits would help, I think.
Vanessa: So do I.

Salesperson: I do too. Let me show you some sets and add ins. That will help expand your wardrobe as quickly and efficiently as possible.
Sally: I see. Then I'll have as many looks as I need.
Salesperson: Exactly. I'll start a dressing room for you. We can start with some timeless outfits. Then we can choose some current extras and accessories.
Vanessa: I don't think we could have chosen a better place to start!
Sally: Neither do I!
Salesperson: We'll start with some plain skirts and pants then find some patterned tops.
Vanessa: I'm just as excited about this as you are!
Sally: Oh, we do love shopping!

We use as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons when the things we are comparing are equal in some way:

This outfit looks just as good as the other one.

We use not as ... as to make comparisons between things which aren't equal:

This jacket doesn't fit as well as the first one.
With office wear, I think comfort is as important as look.
I think I'd like to look as chic as possible without being overdressed.
That will help expand your wardrobe as quickly and efficiently as possible.
Then I'll have as many looks as I need.
This leather jacket is not as expensive as the other one
We us so and neither for positive and negative agreement.

So is used to show agreement with positive statements.
Sometimes we also use too to express the same thing.

Amanda: I like this dress!
Janet: So do I. / I do too.

Neither is used to show agreement with negative statements.
Sometimes we also use either to express the same thing.

Amanda:
I don't think this fits well.
Janet:
Neither do I. (neither is a negative word)
I don't either. (either is used with the negative)
